nodes.label: build_datasets.py - verify, construct, gate, write
nodes.rationale: The step order is deliberate. Verification halts the build rather than warning, because a drifted input would change every reported figure while the datasets still passed their own schema checks. The leakage gates run before packaging because a dataset containing a leak, once written to disk, is a dataset somebody will train on.

nodes.label: Compressed array archive, not a serialised Python object
nodes.rationale: A pickle couples the file to the exact class definitions and library versions that wrote it, so renaming a field or upgrading a library renders it unreadable, and deserialising it executes code, which makes it unsafe to hand to a reviewer.

nodes.label: Checksum-pinned public provenance for every raw input
nodes.rationale: Every raw input is publicly downloadable and verified before use, so the datasets reproduce end to end from published sources. Versioning differs by source: OpenDengue and GADM are frozen citable releases, the influenza matrices are a vendored benchmark verified against an independent mirror, and the Ebola compilation has no version number at all - its checksum is its only version identifier.

nodes.label: loaders/covid_load.py - the one fetched source
nodes.rationale: COVID is fetched from the NYT repository's master branch, a reference that can move by construction, which is exactly why it is pinned. A downloaded source is more exposed to drift than a placed one, not less, so exempting it from the pin would have been backwards. 'Archived upstream' is a reason to expect stability, not a substitute for checking it.

nodes.label: Two alias maps per disease, separated in time
nodes.rationale: The load-time map repairs the case data and must run before aggregation because it reunites units whose series the source split across two spellings; but a load-time alias necessarily rewrites the node identifier, so a shapefile misspelling folded into it propagates into the project's own identifiers. Inverting the entries does not achieve the same thing - it is the separation in time that is required, not a change of direction.

nodes.label: Three obligations the datasets place on the model
nodes.rationale: Add the identity before degree normalisation; keep static covariates out of the shared encoder; refit the scaler at each rolling origin. These are properties of the datasets that cannot be enforced from within them.

nodes.label: Two build environments (base vs conda ebola)
nodes.rationale: Schema unit tests carry no geospatial dependencies and run in seconds; the fixtures are plain text precisely so that this stays true. Everything touching geometry runs in the pinned conda environment.

nodes.label: Where each disease's scaler is fitted
nodes.rationale: Dengue per node on its own country's training cells, influenza per node on the training slice, Ebola pooled over support cells only. The Ebola case is the sharpest: two weeks per node is far too little to estimate a stable per-node scale, and fitting beyond support would leak the outbreak's magnitude into a result presented as few-shot.
